title: OpenFinances
problem: A personal finance app for managing bi-weekly and monthly budgets with fixed and variable income and expenses. Existing apps lacked real-time active cycle detection based on the user's timezone and an installable PWA with live BCCR exchange rates.

decisions.title: Computed cycles, never stored
decisions.description: Date ranges (bi-weekly 1st/2nd half and monthly) are computed in real-time from the current date, not saved to the database. This simplifies the schema and eliminates inconsistencies.

decisions.title: day_of_month for half-month scoping
decisions.description: Fixed items use day_of_month to determine which half-month they apply to: 1-15 only in the 1st half, 16+ only in the 2nd, null applies to all. In monthly mode all fixed items are included.

decisions.title: Timezone via browser cookie
decisions.description: The client sends its offset in minutes via cookie (localTzOffsetMinutes). The server computes ranges in the user's local time, avoiding UTC skew.

decisions.title: Per-user isolation
decisions.description: All data is scoped to the authenticated user. Clients never send user IDs: identity comes from the session (getCurrentUser in auth.ts).

stack.tech: Auth.js v5 (Google OAuth + credentials with scrypt, JWT sessions)

features: Bi-weekly budgets (1st/2nd half) and monthly view
Fixed and variable income/expenses with half-month scoping
Live cycle detection (flips at midnight on day 1 and 16)
Auth: Google OAuth + email/password with open registration
Installable PWA with dark glassmorphism UI, modals and toasts
Live BCCR exchange rates, CRC currency, Spanish UI

title: OpenPaw
problem: A veterinary platform with pet management, shareable digital clinical records, appointments, emergencies, inventory for pet stores, marketplace with cart, services, transfers, approvals, and registration for clinics and stores. The challenge was combining Google authentication, secure secret management, and team coordination with Azure DevOps.

decisions.title: JWT + Google Login
decisions.description: Authentication via JWT for the API and Google Login for quick mobile access. The JWT token is validated on every backend request.

decisions.title: Secrets via env vars (fail-fast)
decisions.description: No secrets in plaintext in the repo. ConnectionStrings, Jwt:Key and Google:ClientId env vars are mandatory: if any is missing, the API starts with an explicit InvalidOperationException.

decisions.title: Azure DevOps Boards
decisions.description: Project management with work boards, reviewed PRs and feature branches. 2-week Scrum workflow with mandatory review.

features: Pet management and shareable digital clinical records
Veterinary appointments and emergency records
Inventory for pet stores
Marketplace with shopping cart, services and transfers
Approval system and clinic/store registration
Dashboard and user profile
JWT + Google Login auth, secrets via env vars with fail-fast
Deployed on Somee/Vercel, managed with Azure DevOps

title: Trustride
problem: A UI prototype for a pet walking app. The goal was to explore the user experience in mobile-first, defining the modular feature-based architecture before building the backend.

decisions.title: Modular feature-based architecture
decisions.description: Each feature (search, profile, bookings) lives in its own folder with dedicated components, hooks, and styles. Enables independent development and testing.

decisions.title: Mobile-first, responsive web
decisions.description: Design optimized for mobile first, with breakpoints that adapt the UI to desktop without breaking the touch experience.

decisions.title: Monorepo ready for backend
decisions.description: Project structure prepared to integrate SQL Server + .NET Core Web API + React+Vite when the backend is defined.

features: UI prototype for pet walking app
Modular feature-based architecture
Mobile-first with responsive web
Structure prepared for backend (.NET + SQL Server)
Deployed on Vercel for interactive testing

title: ISLAVIC
problem: Built for a business in operation, it is an online store with a product catalog. The challenge was delivering a polished interface with React 19, maintaining code quality with strict linting, and deploying quickly to production.

decisions.title: React 19 + Vite for build speed
decisions.description: Vite offers instant HMR and optimized builds. React 19 allows using the latest Server Components and Streaming features.

decisions.title: Oxlint for strict linting
decisions.description: Oxlint as the main linter for quality and consistency rules. Faster than ESLint on large projects.

decisions.title: Deploy on Vercel
decisions.description: Automatic deploy on Vercel with preview per PR. No infrastructure configuration, the business sees the result in minutes.

features: Online store with product catalog
React 19 with latest features
Strict linting with Oxlint
Automatic deploy on Vercel
In use by a real business

title: FlowBank
problem: Checking each bank app for due dates and payment dates is a chore. FlowBank brings the cutoff, payment date, available limit and invoices of all your credit cards into a single panel, unifying debts in colones and dollars.

decisions.title: Next.js 16 App Router + React 19
decisions.description: One framework for landing and dashboard: (public) and (app) routes, SCSS Modules and optimized rendering on Vercel.

decisions.title: Supabase as full backend
decisions.description: Postgres with per-user RLS, Auth and Storage. 9 versioned SQL migrations as the authoritative schema source.

decisions.title: 35 E2E tests with Playwright
decisions.description: Full end-to-end suite over critical flows: auth, cards, invoices and payments. If it is not tested, it is not ready.

decisions.title: Live BCCR exchange rate
decisions.description: Dollar debts convert to colones using the real BCCR rate, cached server-side to respect API limits.

features: Single panel for all credit cards
Cutoff and payment dates per card and bank
Colon and dollar debts with live BCCR conversion
Available limit and invoices per card
Supabase auth with per-user RLS
35 E2E tests with Playwright
